title: A Code of Stars and Tobacco
notes: Detective-cast (Agasa, Conan, Ai Haibara, and the other Detective Boys) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ file's murderer_id (Heihachi Mikami) is confirmed correct by the transcript -- he killed both Asao Kono (a year earlier, over sole credit for a comet discovery) and Hajime Futagawa (present-day, silencing a blackmail attempt). However the old file was thin and, read narrowly, could be misread as Mikami having only killed Futagawa: it left Kono's killer's motive as 'unspecified' and gave no edges at all to Ryoji Amatsuchi, who is actually a major structural figure -- he found Kono's remains, sent the fake invitations under Kono's name that summoned the other three back to the hostel, and sabotaged the phone/cars to trap everyone overnight, but is NOT a murderer (a red herring the transcript briefly leans into before Conan clears him). The old file also collapsed both dying messages into one generic clue node; the transcript actually supports two distinct comparative clues (cigarette-count vs. guestbook kana stroke-count; six-cigarette message vs. seven-cigarette message) which are now separate clue nodes. case_type: murder (two victims, one culprit).

clues.desc: Guestbook kana Kono used for 'mi' takes 6 strokes -- matches the 6 cigarettes in his dying message exactly.
Futagawa's 7-cigarette message (same brand) adds exactly one to Kono's 6 -- both spell Heihachi Mikami, not Futagawa's own initials.
